newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais maintain anti-dumping duty on Ukraine steel.
newsitem.headline: Thais maintain anti-dumping duty on Ukraine steel.

text.p: Thailand has decided to maintain a 45.56 percent anti-dumping tariff on hot-rolled steel sheet from the Ukraine, a commerce ministry official said on Tuesday.
But the ministry reduced the anti-dumping duty on imports of H-beam steel and hot-rolled steel from Poland and Russia, she told Reuters.
The final decision was made on Monday during a meeting to reassess the anti-dumping measures imposed in December last year, the official said.
The government levied the preliminary CIF-based anti-dumping tariff of between 25.59 and 51.99 percent on structural steel from Poland and hot-rolled steel from Ukraine and Russia on December 27.

The move came after Thai governnment studies of dumping allegations by domestic steel firms including structural steel producer, Siam Yamato Co Lts, a unit of Siam Cement Plc and hot-rolled steel producer Sahaviriya Steel Industries Plc .

But after the reassessment, the authorities found that the impact of dumping, or exporting below local market prices, from Ukraine was the strongest while steel dumping from Poland and Russia affected the local industry to a lesser extent, the official said.

Under the new tariff structure, there will be only one rate of anti-dumping tariff on H-beam imports from Poland which is 25.78 percent. Previously, Thailand charged 25.90 percent on the imports from Poland's major steel producer Huta Katowice, 29.81 percent on product from Stalexport and 51.99 percent from other producers, the official said.

The anti-dumping tariff on Russian hot-rolled coil was cut to 25.45, 28.16 and 33.24 percent from 33.92, 34.67 and 43.98 percent respectively. The decision will take immediate effect for five years and the steel exporters in the affected countries can bring up the case for revision one year later, the official said.
